question: The very first translation of the Bhagavad Gita into English was done by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Charles Wilkins.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charles Wilkins **translated the **Bhagavad Gita into English in 1785,** making it the first complete translation of this significant Hindu scripture.
 
• Wilkins's translation helped introduce key concepts of Hindu philosophy, such as **dharma (duty) and yoga (the path to realization)**, to a Western audience, influencing the study of Indian philosophy in Europe.
 
• His translation was completed during the British colonial period, a time marked by growing interest in Oriental studies.
 
• Wilkins utilized a **literal translation approach**, aiming to stay **true to the original Sanskrit text** while making it comprehensible to English readers. 
 
• The translation influenced notable figures such as **Ralph Waldo Emerson and Henry David Thoreau**, who were inspired by the Gita's teachings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Colebrook:**

 
 
• Henry Thomas Colebrook, while an important figure in Indian studies, is known for his **work on Sanskrit grammar** and for translating parts of the** Arthashastra** but did not translate the Bhagavad Gita.
 
 
 
• **William Jones:**
 
 
• An influential figure in the early 19th century, **Jones founded the Asiatic Society in 1784.** He is known for his studies on **Sanskrit **and its relation to European languages but did not complete a translation of the Bhagavad Gita.
 
 
 
• **Max Mueller:**
 
 
• Although a prominent scholar of Indian philosophy and linguistics, Max Mueller’s **contributions included translations of the Rigveda** and other texts, but he was not involved in translating the Bhagavad Gita.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Wilkins:**
 
 
• The impac t of Wilkins’s translation extended beyond academia; it played a** role in the Bengal Renaissance**, influencing thinkers like **Swami Vivekananda** and contributing to the** rise of Indian nationalism.**
